Dear Dr Omar,
Re: Mrs Somarni Khaze, DOB:12/04/1971


I am writing to refer Mrs Khaze, who has been recently diagnosed with moderately differentiated
invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast. Her condition requires your immediate treatment,
including the possibility of urgent reconstructive surgery of her left breast.

Initially, on 22/10/2017, Mrs Khaze presented with an almond-shaped left breast lump, which she
had noticed six weeks ago. She was obese with a BMI of 31. On local examination, her left breast   Commented [OET1]: before: use before instead of ago
was 2*2cm in size, hard and non-tender with ill-defined margins. In addition, palpable mobile      with the past perfect.

axillary lymph nodes were noted.                                                                   Commented [OET2]: the lump




Two weeks later, an Mrs Khaze’s USG revealed an 18*16mm nodule at her left breast with a           Commented [OET3]: You are talking about specific
variable echogenicity. An area of highly suspicious of malignancy at the left breast with and      ultrasound so you should use Mrs Khaze’s

multiple nodules at the axilla were observed on the mammogram. Consequently, she was given         Commented [OET4]: ultrasound: USG is not worldwide
                                                                                                   abbreviation for ultrasound
[counselled on] different treatment options and was advised for a core biopsy.
                                                                                                   Commented [OET5]: with is not wrong but if you write
                                                                                                   “with” then it should be “was observed” instead of “were
                                                                                                   observed”
On today's review, the biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of moderately differentiated invasive
ductal carcinoma of the left breast. Please note that Mrs Khaze has insisted to be operated by
you.


Mrs Khaze has a positive family history of breast carcinoma. She has a past history of a benign
right lump which was treated by a lumpectomy five years ago.

It would be greatly appreciated if you could assess Mrs Khaze's condition and consider an urgent
surgical intervention.

Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any queries.

Yours sincerely,
Dr Tin Aung (GP)

Dear Dr Omar,
Re: Mrs Somarni Khaze, DOB:12/04/1971

I am writing to refer Mrs Khaze, who has been recently diagnosed with moderately differentiated
invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast. Her condition requires your immediate treatment,
including the possibility of urgent reconstructive surgery of her left breast.

Initially, on 22/10/2017, Mrs Khaze presented with an almond-shaped left breast lump, which she
had noticed six weeks ago. She was obese with a BMI of 31. On local examination, her left breast
was 2*2cm in size, hard and non-tender with ill-defined margins. In addition, palpable mobile
axillary lymph nodes were noted.

Two weeks later, an Mrs Khaze’s USG revealed an 18*16mm nodule at her left breast with a
variable echogenicity. An area of highly suspicious of malignancy at the left breast with and
multiple nodules at the axilla were observed on the mammogram. Consequently, she was given
[counselled on] different treatment options and was advised for a core biopsy.

On today's review, the biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of moderately differentiated invasive
ductal carcinoma of the left breast. Please note that Mrs Khaze has insisted to be operated by
you.

Mrs Khaze has a positive family history of breast carcinoma. She has a past history of a benign
right lump which was treated by a lumpectomy five years ago.

It would be greatly appreciated if you could assess Mrs Khaze's condition and consider an urgent
surgical intervention.

Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any queries.

Yours sincerely,
Dr Tin Aung (GP)
